record.body:
## Requirements

R1: `canon export --out FILE` writes one JSON line per op, ordered by record type, record id and seq.
R2: Two exports of the same store are byte-identical.
R3: Each export line holds the record type, record id, seq and the op unchanged.
R4: `canon import FILE` into an empty store appends every op in order and builds `records` and `revisions`.
R5: `canon import` into a non-empty store is rejected and writes nothing.
R6: Import preserves record ids, op ids, seq numbers and `recorded_at` values.
R7: After importing the real file store, folding each chain gives the same revision as `records/<type>/<id>.md`, for every record.
R8: After importing the real file store, every revision that has a file in `history/` has a row in `revisions` with the same hash.
R9: Export from a DB store, then import into an empty DB and export again, gives byte-identical files.
R10: Import fails with a message that names the record when a chain has a gap or a hash mismatch, and writes nothing.
R11: A chain that starts at a checkpoint op imports with its seq numbers unchanged.
R12: `scripts/verify_import.py` exits 0 when R7 and R8 hold and exits 1 on any mismatch, printing the count of records and mismatches.

## Acceptance criteria

- R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R9, R10, R11: unit tests on small temporary stores, including a chain with a checkpoint op and a corrupted chain.
- R7, R8, R12: `scripts/verify_import.py` against a copy of the real store prints `0 mismatches` and exits 0 (command run). A seeded mismatch exits 1 (test).

## Constraints

- Export reads through the `Backend` interface, so it works for both backends until cutover.
- Import is one transaction.
- Export is plain JSONL and needs no tool other than `canon`.

## Non-goals

- Switching this repo to the DB.
- Merging an export into a non-empty store. `canon merge` covers store-to-store merges.
- Wiring a backup hook.

## Invariants

- Import never rewrites an op.
- An export contains no timestamp of the export itself.

## Assumptions

- The real store has about 9,100 records and 10,000 op files. Import fits in one transaction.
- Some chains start at a checkpoint op because `prune_before` removed older ops. The checkpoint holds the full state.
